canDo: Can build a clearly structured argumentative essay with d’abord/ensuite/enfin, d’une part… d’autre part, en outre/par ailleurs, quant à, certes… mais, en revanche, autrement dit, bref/en définitive, and use connectors to predict where an argument is going when reading and listening.
review: Review day 7’s concessions (bien que, même si, pourtant), day 6’s consequence expressions and day 5’s cause expressions; today, fit them into a “text skeleton”: introduction – argument – concession – rebuttal – conclusion.
input: Read: an article assessing digital tools in schools, a column against a “blanket” phone ban and a notice of a school’s digital charter — mark the connectors in each paragraph and write an outline of the whole text; listen: a debate on coding in primary school, a segment defending handwriting and a news flash about handing out refurbished computers — when you hear certes, en revanche or quant à, predict where the next sentence is going.
output: Write: an argumentative article for a school magazine, “AI in schools: threat or ally?” (≥220 words), with at least one text connector per paragraph; speak: a 4-minute structured monologue on “parents seeing grades in real time”, then a debate on “replacing paper textbooks entirely with digital ones”.
checkpoint: Reading + listening accuracy ≥80%; at least 6 different connectors used correctly in the article (certes must be followed by mais/toutefois); in the first 30 seconds of the monologue, clearly announce a two- or three-part outline.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a news item on TV5MONDE or RFI’s « Journal en français facile » about schools, screens or AI, and write 3 sentences of comment with « Certes…, mais… », « D’une part…, d’autre part… » and « Quant à… »; then record 1 minute of audio, starting by announcing your two-point outline.

questions.why: « La réalité est plus nuancée, et elle mérite d’être examinée point par point », and the whole text assesses each point in turn with d’abord / ensuite / quant à / en définitive. B is too absolute — the author is against “throwing it all out”; C isn’t mentioned.
« Sur le second point [individualiser], les résultats sont plutôt encourageants »; as for motivation, « en revanche, l’effet s’est vite dissipé » (A is wrong).
Certes first concedes that “it’s hard to blame school screens for everything”, then Mais argues that schools may still have reinforced fragmented reading — a classic concessive structure.
ne… que par = only depends on: a tool’s value depends entirely on how it is used in teaching. B takes valoir to mean price; C over-negates.
« Plutôt qu’une interdiction, une éducation. » C is wrong: he grants that notifications disrupt lessons and that social media fuel bullying.
Certes introduces the ban supporters’ reasons (disrupted lessons, bullying), which Mais then rebuts.
« ils n’ont pas vocation à jouer les policiers » — it isn’t their job.
This is a rhetorical question; the previous sentence, « les adultes devraient être cohérents », shows adults can’t manage it themselves.
« Quant aux élèves qui ne disposent pas d’un ordinateur… ils pourront en emprunter un » — a measure addressing unequal access to devices at home.
« décomposer le problème en étapes, anticiper, corriger ses erreurs… il fait des mathématiques et de la logique ». B is exactly the argument Nadia rebuts.
« je conteste l’argument… selon lequel il faudrait coder tôt pour trouver un emploi plus tard »; B is something she actually « reconnais volontiers ».
« renoncer à l’écriture manuscrite serait une erreur ». B is the opposite; C isn’t mentioned.
« on ne peut pas tout recopier : on est obligé de reformuler, de choisir l’essentiel »; B is the opposite.
« apprenons les deux, mais dans le bon ordre : le stylo d’abord, le clavier ensuite »; A is rejected with « Pas du tout ! ».

V23-03.exZh: Once the novelty wore off, the pupils’ enthusiasm faded.

V23-06.exZh: These online exercises only work under a teacher’s guidance.

V23-07.exZh: A tool’s value depends entirely on its educational use.

V23-08.exZh: The author is against an outright ban on phones in secondary schools.

V23-09.exZh: A rule is useless if nobody can enforce it.

V23-10.exZh: The supervisors are overwhelmed and can’t check every pupil.

V23-12.exZh: I refuse to play the police officer at the start of every lesson.

V23-13.exZh: The charter was drawn up by a working group of parents and pupils.

V23-15.exZh: Homework is handed in on the school’s digital platform.

V23-21.exZh: I prefer a pen to a keyboard, and I’m not ashamed of it!

V23-23.exZh: The AI assistant made a glaring mistake, and the pupil didn’t notice.

title: Organising a text
